Fiberglass Coated Veil for Mineral Wool Roof Insulation

A coated fiberglass facing for mineral wool insulation boards in pitched roofs. Select water resistance and vapor permeability for your core, lamination process and complete roof assembly.

Material options Applications Specifications FAQ

What Challenges Does Mineral Wool Face Beneath a Pitched Roof?

01

Surface wetting

Condensation, installation moisture or accidental water exposure can introduce moisture at the insulation surface.

02

Restricted drying

Unsuitable vapor control can trap moisture and reduce the intended drying potential of the roof construction.

03

Fiber disturbance

Transport, handling and installation can abrade or damage an unprotected mineral wool surface.

04

Facing delamination

Adhesive, coating and process incompatibility can weaken the facing-to-core bond.

For pitched roof insulation systems, select a facing for mineral wool roof insulation boards according to temperature, humidity and incidental wetting.

A Protective Facing for More Reliable Roof Insulation

Liquid-water resistance

Selected coatings help reduce direct liquid water penetration through the facing under specified conditions.

Moisture management

Evaluate water resistance and vapor permeability independently against the roof assembly's requirements.

Lamination and handling

Check coating, substrate and adhesive compatibility for surface protection, dimensional stability and consistent conversion.

Select coating and substrate for the roof construction, lamination method and handling conditions of your mineral wool boards.

Different Roof Designs. Different Facing Requirements.

Compare material descriptions
01

Standard coated veil

A uniform surface for conventional mineral wool boards, with stable handling and consistent processing.

02

Moisture-resistant coated veil

A selected coating can reduce liquid water penetration through the exposed facing. Evaluate it for boards needing additional protection against incidental moisture exposure.

03

Vapor-permeable coated veil

Select vapor transmission for the construction's drying strategy, then confirm the grade with the complete pitched roof assembly.

Choose the facing according to water exposure, drying strategy, mineral wool core and production requirements.

A Thin Facing. An Important Protective Surface.

Coated fiberglass veil

A lightweight substrate with selectable coating properties for water resistance, vapor permeability and core compatibility.

Mineral wool insulation core

Assess facing and core as a complete board for adhesive bonding, dimensional stability, moisture behavior and relevant finished-board performance.

The facing forms a protective surface layer. Mineral wool provides the board's primary thermal insulation function and may contribute to roof-assembly acoustic and fire performance.

Designed for Mineral Wool Insulation in Pitched Roofs

Between-rafter insulation

A stable surface can support board handling in sloped roof cavities. Select moisture properties for the roof's vapor-control and drying strategy.

Above-rafter insulation

Facing options support surface control and lamination of suitable boards in continuous insulation layers.

Roof retrofit

A stable facing can support handling and material integrity for suitable mineral wool products used within existing roof structures.

Prefabricated roof panels

Customizable facing properties support evaluation of dimensionally consistent boards and integration with factory-made panel components.

The finished roof assembly must include the appropriate weatherproofing, structural support, and moisture-control components.

Evaluate suitable boards for the intended residential or light commercial roof construction.

Use the intended mineral wool core, adhesive system and production process in the trial.

Questions Manufacturers Ask Before Choosing a Mineral Wool Facer

Does the facing make the roof moisture-proof?

Selected grades can reduce direct liquid water penetration. Finished-system moisture performance also depends on the core, joints, membranes and roof design.

Can the facing guarantee mold prevention?

Moisture-resistant facing may help limit certain forms of surface wetting. However, mold prevention depends on the complete roof assembly, including moisture control, condensation management, ventilation, and adjacent materials. The facing alone cannot guarantee mold prevention.

Is lower vapor transmission always better?

Not necessarily. A roof needs an appropriate balance of water resistance and vapor management. Restricting transmission may be unsuitable where it limits intended drying.

Can the same grade suit different roof configurations?

Evaluate suitability for the board design, installation method, moisture strategy and applicable building requirements. Coating, basis weight and width can be discussed for the core and process.
